title: Annual Estimates of the Resident Population for Incorporated Places in Georgia, Vintage 2025 (sub-est2025_13)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program
geography: Georgia state, counties and incorporated places (including consolidated-government balances)
measures: Estimates base 2020 and July 1 population estimates 2020–2025 for Georgia, Atlanta city, Savannah city, Augusta-Richmond County consolidated government (balance), Columbus city, Athens-Clarke County unified government (balance), and counties.
limitations: Model-based estimates revised each vintage; change figures on pages are derived from base 2020 and July 2025 values.

title: Annual Resident Population Estimates for Metropolitan and Micropolitan Statistical Areas and Their Counties, Vintage 2025 (cbsa-est2025-alldata)
publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program
geography: Atlanta-Sandy Springs-Roswell, Savannah, Augusta-Richmond County (GA-SC), Columbus (GA-AL) and Athens-Clarke County metro areas and their component counties
measures: Metro and component-county population estimates; also lists the counties that make up each metro area.
limitations: Model-based estimates; metro delineations follow the OMB definitions used for Vintage 2025.

title: Rule 150-10-.01 Fraudulent, Misleading or Deceptive Advertising (Chapter 150-10 Advertising)
publisher: Georgia Board of Dentistry, Rules and Regulations of the State of Georgia (Georgia Secretary of State)
measures: Definition of advertising; dentist responsibility for ads placed by agents; one-year retention of ad copies; fee-advertising conditions (full min/max disclosure for ranges, 60-day availability, "free" offers, required related-charges statement); patient-information consent; statements deemed misleading (superiority, unrecognised specialist claims, practising at a location not regularly served, "quality dentistry", "latest modern equipment", painless claims, confusingly similar trade names).
limitations: Text as displayed on the retrieval date; the page did not show an effective date. Not legal advice; practices should confirm current rules with counsel.

title: Fort Benning (official installation website)
measures: Current official installation name "U.S. Army Fort Benning".
limitations: Home page; used only to confirm the current name.

title: Fort Gordon, GA (official installation website)
measures: Current official installation name "U.S. Army Fort Gordon".
limitations: Home page; used only to confirm the current name.

title: About Fort Stewart-Hunter Army Airfield
measures: Stewart-Hunter employs over 25,500 people; 21,200 full-time Soldiers, 4,350 Army civilian workers and contractors and more than 19,000 military retirees call Stewart-Hunter communities home; Hunter Army Airfield is in Savannah.
limitations: Installation-reported figures; undated page; covers Fort Stewart (Hinesville) and Hunter Army Airfield together.

title: Fort Benning takes back its old name, but to honor a different soldier
measures: Army restored the Fort Benning name (from Fort Moore) at a ceremony at the base just outside Columbus; roughly 70,000 soldiers, civilian workers and military family members are stationed at Fort Benning.
limitations: News report; the 70,000 figure is as reported by AP in April 2025.

title: After quick switch, signs say ‘Fort Gordon’ again at local Army post
measures: Augusta Army post known as Fort Eisenhower for about a year and a half became Fort Gordon again in June 2025; home of the Army Cyber Center of Excellence.
limitations: Local news report.

title: Dental Care
measures: Dental coverage by beneficiary type: active duty service members covered by active duty dental benefits; active duty family members can purchase the TRICARE Dental Program; retirees and families may be eligible for FEDVIP Dental.
limitations: Page shows "Last Updated 3/30/2020"; benefit details should be confirmed on the current TRICARE site.

title: TRICARE Dental Program
measures: United Concordia administers the TRICARE Dental Program; enrollees find CONUS dentists through the United Concordia network.
limitations: Program contractor and terms can change.

title: Heritage — Dental College of Georgia
measures: Describes the Dental College of Georgia as Georgia's only dental school, part of Augusta University in Augusta.
limitations: Institutional page.

title: AU breaks ground on new Dental College of Georgia campus in Savannah
measures: DCG Savannah on the Armstrong Campus of Georgia Southern University is slated to open in summer 2028; DCG has about 400 dental students and 60 dental hygiene students enrolled each year; the release states Georgia ranks 46th nationally in dentists per capita and 18 counties have no practicing dentist.
limitations: University news release; the per-capita ranking and county count are the university's figures, not independently verified here. Publication date taken from the page text.

title: UGA enrolls record number of Georgians
measures: UGA total enrollment reached 43,888 in fall 2025, up 1.7% from the prior year; Georgians are 83% of undergraduates.
limitations: Enrollment count, not the number of students living in Athens-Clarke County year-round.

title: Columbus Consolidated Government (official website)
measures: States that Columbus Consolidated Government is Georgia's first consolidated government.
limitations: Home page text; used only for the government's description of itself.

title: Athens-Clarke County, GA — Official Website
measures: Official name "Athens-Clarke County Unified Government" (ACCGov).
limitations: Home page; used only for the official name.

title: Hyundai produces first vehicle, IONIQ 5, at Bryan Co. Metaplant
measures: Hyundai Motor Group Metaplant America in Bryan County began producing vehicles in October 2024; described as Georgia's largest economic development deal.
limitations: News report; no employment or relocation figures are used from it.
